cited_evidence: Top-level input includes record_id n06-r01 with demand_score 9 and need "isolate faulty execution branches before replay".
Behavioural criteria require selecting all qualifying or fallback demand records and retaining allowed record identities without silently omitting stipulated records.
Job 1 output handed to Job 2 contains needs n06-r02 through n06-r08 only; n06-r01 is absent and metadata record_count is effectively reflected as seven downstream records.

In generated/protocol_2_2/upstream_demand_provenance.py, select_demand selects demand_score >= 3, but normalize defines allowed_record_ids as ['n06-r09', 'n06-r02', 'n06-r03', 'n06-r04', 'n06-r05', 'n06-r06', 'n06-r07', 'n06-r08'], excluding n06-r01.
initial_receipt.explanation: The two-job execution is faulty because qualifying demand record n06-r01 was silently omitted before the downstream handoff. The top-level corpus contains n06-r01 with demand_score 9, so it qualifies under the demand_score >= 3 selection rule. Job 1's observed handoff starts at n06-r02 and contains only seven records, so Job 2 can only preserve the incomplete upstream input it received. The supplied Job 1 code localizes the omission to normalize: its allowed_record_ids list excludes n06-r01 and instead includes n06-r09, causing n06-r01 to be filtered out after selection.
